label: prop:coxeter-strong-exchange
title: Strong exchange for Coxeter systems, via the reflection cocycle
html:
Proposition. Strong exchange for Coxeter systems, via the reflection cocycle

Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system with length function \ell, let \omega = (s_{i_1}, \dots, s_{i_k}) be any word in the generators (not necessarily reduced), and let t be a reflection of W with \ell(\pi(\omega)\, t) < \ell(\pi(\omega)), where \pi(\omega) denotes the product of the word. Then some single letter of \omega can be deleted: there is an index j < k with

\pi(\omega)\, t \;=\; \pi(\omega \setminus j),

where \omega \setminus j is the word with its j-th letter erased.

The proof is the classical reflection-cocycle construction. Each generator s acts on W \times \mathbb{Z}/2 by (w, \varepsilon) \mapsto (s w s,\; \varepsilon + [w = s]); these involutions satisfy the Coxeter relations because the inversion sequence of the doubled braid word consists of two identical halves, so every \mathbb{Z}/2 parity count cancels. The resulting homomorphism W \to \mathrm{Perm}(W \times \mathbb{Z}/2) makes the parity \eta(w, t) of the number of occurrences of t in the right inversion sequence independent of the chosen word for w. The cocycle law gives \eta(t, t) = 1 for every reflection, hence \eta(wt, t) = 1 + \eta(w, t), and a length descent forces \eta(w, t) = 1; a positive parity locates an occurrence of t in the inversion sequence, and deleting that letter realises the product. No induction on length and no reduced-word hypothesis is needed.
